facts.text: Browerville first settled in 1865 by John Bassett near the Long Prairie River, then relocated in 1869 to a new site to accommodate the Great Northern Railroad.
The city was platted in 1882 and named after Jacob V., a pioneer who helped establish the community.
Browerville is the birthplace of bestselling author LaVyrle Spencer, known for her contemporary and historical romance novels.
Two buildings in town are on the National Register of Historic Places: the 1883 Kahlert Mercantile Store and the Church of St.
In the early 20th century, a Rusyn farming community settled in Browerville, leading to the founding of a Byzantine Catholic parish and a Greek Catholic Union chapter.
The Long Prairie River flows near Browerville’s eastern boundary, shaping the town’s early settlement patterns.
